inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E adjusted net sales (ex manufactured-PFAS products, exited end-2025): FY2025 adjusted 24,279 (10-K non-GAAP table) + 9M-2026 adjusted 19,087 actual (+4.5% on 18,256) + Q4 estimated at ~6,340 (Q4-2025 adjusted 6,023 x ~1.055 incl. ~90-100 of Madison). Ties to guidance of adjusted sales growth >4.5%. GAAP FY2025 revenue was 24,948; TTM GAAP to Sep-2026 is 25,247.
inputs.share_count_basis: 516.73m shares outstanding at 2026-09-30 (10-Q balance sheet) + 3.8m dilution from stock plans (Q3-2026 EPS note) = 520.5m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. 3M is a heavy net repurchaser (3,225 in 9M-2026 vs ~215 SBC), so the flat count is funded many times over and is conservative relative to the actual ~3%/yr shrink; the excess buyback is treated as value-neutral capital return.
inputs.net_debt_note: Short-term borrowings and current LTD 2,439 + long-term debt 12,558 = 14,997 (includes the 1,430 Sentorum venture term loan and the Sep-2026 EUR 1.5bn notes). Cash 4,835 + current marketable securities 310 = 5,145. Operating leases (~0.55bn) are excluded: under US GAAP the operating lease cost is already inside EBITDA.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Company-defined ADJUSTED free cash flow guided for FY2026 (~4.8bn; adjusted OCF ~5.9bn, capex ~1.0bn), which excludes significant-litigation and PFAS-exit payments. GAAP FCF is far lower because of settlement payments: FY2025 1,396 (OCF 2,306 - capex 910); TTM to Sep-2026 2,677 (OCF 3,629 - capex 952) after ~2.0bn of net litigation/PFAS payments in 9M-2026. The adjusted figure is the right run-rate base ONLY because the accrued settlement liabilities are deducted separately in equity_bridge. Note it is a levered figure (after ~0.45bn net cash interest); the model's flows are unlevered.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net debt, not net cash, so no strip is required; the component build starts from operating EBITDA and never includes the ~170/yr of interest income (127 in 9M-2026).
inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3-2026 cash flow statement: stock-based compensation expense 167 for 9M-2026 (182 in 9M-2025); FY2025 10-K cash flow 211 (FY2024 273, FY2023 265). FY2026E ~215. 3M publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure; equity-award tax withholding is not separately disclosed and is small, so the cash-flow add-back is used.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual purchases of treasury stock, 9M-2026 (financing activities); FY2025 3,251. ~1.5bn remained on the Feb-2025 7.5bn program at 2026-09-30; a new 6bn authorization followed in Nov-2026 (authorization, not spend).
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is the FY2026 guidance year (nine months actual), so Y1 = FY2027 and Y10 = FY2036. Chosen over FY2025-as-FY0 because the valuation date is six weeks before year-end and the Sep-2026 balance sheet already reflects nine months of FY2026 cash flow (spent on buybacks that shrank the share count used here); making FY2026 year 1 would count those flows twice. Q4-2026 cash generation is ignored, a small conservatism.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.0 = ~9.3% cost of equity; pre-tax debt ~5.2% (A3/BBB+/A-), ~4.1% after tax; ~88/12 equity/debt at market gives ~8.7%, rounded to 8.5%. The SAME 8.5% is used in all three scenarios: PFAS/litigation and cyclical risk are charged in the flows, the equity bridge and the scenario weights, not by stacking a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), by construction: US GAAP operating lease cost (~200/yr cash) is an operating expense inside EBITDA, and lease liabilities are excluded from net debt. No separate lease path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are fully consolidated; minorities are deducted once, in the equity bridge: Bain's redeemable interest in the 3M Sentorum (Fire Safety and Rescue) venture at carrying/redemption value, and the 25% public minority in 3M India Ltd at market value.
inputs.litigation_treatment: Charged once, in three layers that do not overlap. (1) ACCRUED settlements (PWS/other PFAS environmental 7.5bn, Combat Arms 1.1bn, non-Aearo respirator/asbestos 0.44bn; already discounted present values on the balance sheet) are deducted after tax in equity_bridge, and the flows are therefore built on the adjusted, ex-litigation-payment basis. (2) UNACCRUED exposure (AFFF personal injury, state AG suits, turnout-gear MDL, Europe/Zwijndrecht) is a 2.5bn after-tax judgment allowance in the bridge for all scenarios. (3) The bear case alone carries a further ~1.5pp EBITDA-margin drag for a second PWS-scale wave. Recurring transformation/restructuring cost that management excludes from adjusted income (224 in 9M-2026) is put back into the margin path.
inputs.solventum_spin_treatment: Health Care (Solventum) was spun 2024-04-01 and is discontinued operations. Forward drivers are anchored only on post-spin continuing operations (FY2024-FY2026 adjusted). FY2022/FY2023 revenue in the Metrics CSV is restated continuing-ops; FY2021 and earlier, and FY2023-and-earlier cash flow, capex, D&A and equity, are pre-spin consolidated and are NOT comparable. The retained ~15% Solventum stake is a bridge asset at fair value; its mark-to-market is excluded from the flows.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios, via the Drivers route. Routed by dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical: industrials' (owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md for the NCI, non-operating-asset, lease and charge-risk-once rules). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Working capital is modelled as a CONSUMER of cash on growth (receivables 4,116 + inventory 4,081 - payables 3,040 = ~20% of sales). Price is a regular-session close, not an extended-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: adjusted organic sales growth trend (FY2024 +1.2%, FY2025 +2.1%, 9M-2026 +3.3%), not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every trailing CAGR is distorted and none is usable as a growth anchor. FY2025 vs FY2022/FY2020 endpoints: the 5-year figures straddle the April-2024 Solventum spin (FY2020 revenue 32,184 and equity 12,931 are pre-spin consolidated; FY2022 revenue 26,161 is restated continuing ops, so only the 3-year revenue CAGR is like-for-like, and it includes the PFAS-product exit). Equity fell from 14,770 to 4,747 on the 2023 PWS and Combat Arms charges (~14.5bn pre-tax) and the spin distribution, so equity CAGR diverges far more than 30% from revenue and the house 'equity CAGR first' rule is set aside. EPS is GAAP (FY2025 6.00 vs adjusted 8.06).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC): FY2025 1,396 - 211 = 1,185; FY2022 3,842 - 263 = 3,579; FY2020 6,612 - 262 = 6,350. FY2024-FY2025 GAAP FCF is depressed by settlement payments and earlier years include Health Care, so the decline is not an operating trend. SBC is small (~0.85% of sales) and falling, so owner and reported FCF trends do not diverge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 = ~3.0% organic plus ~0.7pp from the first-half carry of Madison Fire & Rescue (closed July 2026, ~90/quarter). Thereafter organic growth fades from 3% toward 2.5%: above the flat decade before the turnaround, below the current 3.3-3.5% run-rate.
base.margin_rationale: EBITDA before SBC. FY2026E anchor ~30.4%: adjusted operating income ~24.9% of adjusted sales (9M 25.2%, Q4 seasonally lower) + D&A not already added back (~1,340 total less ~150 acquisition amortization that the new non-GAAP basis excludes) + SBC 0.85%. From that, ~1.0pp is deducted for transformation/restructuring cost and legal defence that management treats as special (transformation was 224 in 9M-2026), fading to ~0.5pp as the program ends, while productivity adds ~0.4pp/yr until adjusted operating margin reaches ~26.5%.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guide ~1.0bn (3.9%); FY2025 3.6%, pre-spin norm 4.5-5%. Drifts up to 4.5% so terminal capex is not run below a sustainable level; terminal D&A stays above capex only by the acquired-intangible amortization.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted effective rate 19.5-19.9% (9M-2026, FY2025); cash taxes 800-850 in FY2024-25 are flattered by settlement deductions, whose shield is already inside the after-tax bridge items. Ramps to 21%.

bear.margin_rationale: Includes ~1.5pp (~0.4bn/yr pre-tax) of additional PFAS settlement cash through year 8, i.e. roughly 3bn nominal beyond the bridge allowance, plus an industrial downturn in year 2 and lost operating leverage.

scenario_narratives.base: The Brown turnaround holds but stops compounding at its 2025-26 pace. Organic growth settles at ~3% (Safety and Industrial and semiconductor/data-center/aerospace exposure in Transportation and Electronics offsetting a flat Consumer segment), then fades to 2.5%. Adjusted operating margin edges from ~25% to ~26.5%, but the transformation and restructuring spend that management excludes is treated as a real, slowly fading cost. Capex normalises upward from today's 3.9% of sales. PFAS and Combat Arms cost what is accrued today plus a 2.5bn after-tax allowance for the personal-injury, state AG and turnout-gear claims that are not yet accrued. The Solventum stake is sold at about today's value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround is structural: 1,000 new products and commercial excellence lift organic growth to 4-5% for five years, with data-center, semiconductor and aerospace demand doing much of the work and Madison/Sentorum adding a faster-growing fire-safety franchise. Productivity and on-time-in-full gains take EBITDA margin to 33.5% (adjusted operating margin ~28.5%, in line with the best multi-industrials). The AFFF personal-injury docket settles inside the bridge allowance, and the PFAS manufacturing exit proves to have capped the liability. The terminal multiple re-rates modestly to 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: PFAS is not bounded. A second wave of settlements (AFFF personal injury, state attorneys-general, turnout gear, European remediation) costs roughly another 3bn nominal beyond the allowance, paid over eight years, and keeps the stock at a liability-discount multiple (14x). An industrial and consumer downturn in FY2028 cuts sales 3% in a company that lost diversification with Solventum, tariffs and dis-synergies compress margins, and part of the recent adjusted-margin gain proves to be accounting reclassification (the amortization change) and deferred investment, so capex has to rise toward 4.8% of sales. Growth recovers only to 1.5%, matching the pre-turnaround decade.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25% because the PFAS exposure is explicitly unbounded in the filings (3M states it cannot estimate a loss range beyond accruals, and a new MDL formed as recently as August 2026) and the business is more cyclical post-spin. Base held at 50%: guidance has been raised twice in 2026 and the accrued settlements are on a fixed schedule. Bull cut to 25% because it needs three independent things at once: sustained 4-5% organic growth from a company that was flat for a decade, peer-leading margins, and litigation closing inside the allowance.

valuation_philosophy.summary: 3M is valued as a mature, high-margin industrial on unlevered owner FCF built from adjusted (ex-litigation-payment) operating components, with the legacy liabilities taken out of the equity bridge at their accrued, after-tax present value rather than left to depress the flows indefinitely. That split is the central judgment: the operating business is worth far more than GAAP cash flow of recent years suggests, and the liabilities are worth far more than zero. Management's 'adjusted' exclusions are not all accepted: recurring transformation cost is put back into the margin path. Risk is charged through the bridge allowance, the bear-case margin drag and a 25% bear weight, with one WACC for all scenarios.
key_risks_to_valuation: PFAS liability beyond accruals: every 1bn of additional after-tax cost is ~$1.9 per share; the 2.5bn allowance is a judgment, not a disclosed figure
Tax deductibility of settlement payments (22% assumed) and uncounted insurance recoveries cut in opposite directions on ~9bn of accrued liabilities
Quality of adjusted margins: ~40bp of the 2026 gain came from a non-GAAP amortization methodology change, and transformation costs (224 in 9M-2026) are excluded by management
Terminal value is cap-bound at 17x in the base case; the market is paying a higher multiple of current unlevered FCF, so the gap to price is largely a multiple and duration disagreement
FY0 is an estimate (FY2026E, nine months actual); the Sep-2026 balance sheet excludes Q4 cash flow, Q4 buybacks and the final PWS claims-administrator determination of the 10.5-12.5bn range
Solventum stake (2.25bn) and the 3M India minority (0.85bn) are marked to market and will move with those share prices
